title: The Limits of China’s Self-Sufficiency
gist: Teaser excerpt only: argues that China's dependence on soybean imports is an under-appreciated vulnerability that could deter a war over Taiwan, alongside the commonly cited risks of military defeat, economic slowdown and restricted oil/tech imports. Xi Jinping listed food security first among national-security priorities at the 2022 20th Party Congress.

themes.theme: Food insecurity as a Taiwan deterrent

insights.claim: China's reliance on soybean imports is an often-overlooked vulnerability that could weigh against a conflict in the Taiwan Strait, as significant as military defeat, economic slowdown or restricted oil and technology imports.
insights.speaker: Joel Wuthnow
insights.so_what: Soybean import flows and Chinese stockpiling are a potential leading indicator of Taiwan conflict preparation.
insights.quote: an equally significant vulnerability is often left off the list: China’s reliance on soybean imports
